---
title: "Conditional independence"
---

The foundations chapter defined [independence for events](../foundations/independence.qmd), and the preceding pages extended probability to [joint distributions](joint-probability.qmd). We now ask whether two variables are independent after conditioning on a third. Suppose a corpus records subject omission $O$, verb final order $V$, and clause type $C$.

[**Conditional independence**](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-intro.html) states that two variables are independent within every relevant value of a conditioning variable.

We write

$$
O\perp\!\!\!\perp V\mid C
$$

and read the statement as “$O$ is independent of $V$ given $C$.”

## Constructing an independent table for main clauses

Within main clauses, suppose

$$
\mathbb{P}(O=1\mid C=\mathrm{main})=.80
$$

and

$$
\mathbb{P}(V=1\mid C=\mathrm{main})=.75.
$$

If $O$ and $V$ are independent within this clause type, the joint target probability is

$$
.80(.75)=.60.
$$

The full conditional joint PMF is

| main clauses | $V=0$ | $V=1$ | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $O=0$ | $.05$ | $.15$ | $.20$ |
| $O=1$ | $.20$ | $.60$ | $.80$ |
| total | $.25$ | $.75$ | $1$ |

Every cell equals its row margin times its column margin.

## Constructing an independent table for subordinate clauses

Within subordinate clauses, suppose

$$
\mathbb{P}(O=1\mid C=\mathrm{sub})=.20
$$

and

$$
\mathbb{P}(V=1\mid C=\mathrm{sub})=.25.
$$

The joint target probability under conditional independence is $.20(.25)=.05$.

| subordinate clauses | $V=0$ | $V=1$ | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $O=0$ | $.60$ | $.20$ | $.80$ |
| $O=1$ | $.15$ | $.05$ | $.20$ |
| total | $.75$ | $.25$ | $1$ |

Again, every cell factors into the corresponding conditional margins.

## Stating the conditional factorization

For every relevant clause type $c$, conditional independence requires

$$
p_{O,V\mid C}(o,v\mid c)
=p_{O\mid C}(o\mid c)p_{V\mid C}(v\mid c).
$$

An equivalent statement is

$$
p_{O\mid V,C}(o\mid v,c)
=p_{O\mid C}(o\mid c).
$$

Once clause type is known, learning verb order does not change the conditional distribution of subject omission.

## Pooling the clause types

Suppose main and subordinate clauses each receive probability $.50$. Averaging corresponding cells across the two tables gives

| pooled clauses | $V=0$ | $V=1$ | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $O=0$ | $.325$ | $.175$ | $.50$ |
| $O=1$ | $.175$ | $.325$ | $.50$ |
| total | $.50$ | $.50$ | $1$ |

In the pooled table,

$$
\mathbb{P}(O=1,V=1)=.325.
$$

The product of the pooled margins is

$$
\mathbb{P}(O=1)\mathbb{P}(V=1)
=.50(.50)
=.25.
$$

Since $.325\neq.25$, the variables are dependent before conditioning on clause type.

Main clauses have high probabilities for both properties, while subordinate clauses have low probabilities for both. Mixing clause types produces a pooled association even though the properties are independent within each type.

## Verifying one stratum in base R

```{r}
#| eval: false
main <- matrix(c(.05, .20, .15, .60), nrow = 2)
subordinate <- matrix(c(.60, .15, .20, .05), nrow = 2)
pooled <- .50 * main + .50 * subordinate

main[2, 2]
sum(main[2, ]) * sum(main[, 2])
pooled
```

The first two results both equal `.60`, verifying one main clause cell. The pooled matrix shows the induced association.

## Conditional and unconditional claims differ

The example establishes that

$$
O\perp\!\!\!\perp V\mid C
$$

does not imply

$$
O\perp\!\!\!\perp V.
$$

The reverse implication also need not hold. An independence claim is incomplete unless it states which variables are conditioned on.

## Stating the conditioning set

A conditional independence claim must state its conditioning set. Saying “subject omission is independent of verb order” erases the fact that the equality holds only within clause types in this model.

Include the vertical bar in notation and prose: independent given clause type.

## Check your understanding

1. Verify the cell $\mathbb{P}(O=0,V=1\mid C=\mathrm{main})=.15$ from its margins.
2. Compute $\mathbb{P}(O=1\mid V=1,C=\mathrm{sub})$ and compare it with $\mathbb{P}(O=1\mid C=\mathrm{sub})$.
3. Why are $O$ and $V$ dependent in the pooled table?
4. State precisely which independence claim the two stratum tables support.

Conditional independence concerns complete distributions within groups. The [next page](conditional-expectation.qmd) summarizes the center of a response distribution within each condition.
